Welcome to AirNudge\n\nControl Android with deliberate hand gestures. AirNudge is assistive input—not a replacement for the touchscreen in safety-critical situations.

Gesture tutorial

Swipe your hand up, down, left, or right to scroll. Make a closed fist for Back. With Air Cursor enabled, move your index fingertip to position the pointer and pinch to tap.

Keep gestures deliberate and return to a neutral hand between actions.

Private by design\n\nCamera access is required to detect your hand. Frames should be analyzed on device and are not needed by the accessibility service. AirNudge does not retrieve screen content and does not use app-specific APIs.

Accessibility permission\n\nAndroid requires this service to send swipes, Back, and taps. AirNudge cannot enable it for you. Select “AirNudge gesture control” in system settings, review Android’s disclosure, then return here.

Enable Air Cursor, then move your fingertip toward each screen edge. Increase sensitivity if you cannot reach an edge. Add only enough smoothing to control jitter; lower smoothing responds faster. Changes apply immediately.
Balanced is the default. Compare AirNudgePerformance logs on your device before choosing a faster or lower-power profile.
Move the pointer with the normalized index-fingertip position. Pinch taps at its current location.
